headline: Full Stack Developer Salary in the United States 2026: Average Pay by Level and City
metaDescription: Full stack developer salary in the US 2026: national average near $136,000, junior to senior ranges, top-paying cities, and the skills that raise pay.

sections.content:
Full stack developers in the United States earn an average base salary of about $136,000 in 2026, according to Indeed's June 2026 data drawn from roughly 14,000 job postings, with a typical $5,500 annual cash bonus on top. Glassdoor puts the average base closer to $119,000, while ZipRecruiter reports around $123,000 with a 90th percentile near $164,500. The sources disagree because they measure different things: aggregators of job postings capture broad base pay, while total-compensation surveys of tech employers run past $162,000 once bonus and equity are included.

Entry-level full stack roles typically start between $60,000 and $95,000, depending on the city and stack. Senior engineers command roughly $130,000 to $195,000 in base pay, and total compensation at tech-heavy employers can reach $170,000 or more when equity and bonuses are counted. The Bureau of Labor Statistics projects software developer employment to grow about 15 percent through 2034, well above the average for all occupations.
sections.title: 2026 Salary Benchmarks by Source

sections.content:
San Francisco remains the highest-paying market at roughly $183,000 a year, followed by New York at about $164,000. McLean, Virginia pays near $166,000 thanks to its concentration of defense and federal tech employers, while Charlotte, North Carolina averages around $145,600 and Irving, Texas about $144,600. Washington, DC sits near $142,600.

The gap between top and mid-tier markets reflects cost of living and employer mix more than skill differences. Remote work has narrowed the spread for mid-career developers, and many companies now pay location-adjusted salaries that land between national and Bay Area levels. When comparing offers, weigh total compensation against housing costs: a $150,000 salary in a mid-cost city often leaves more after rent than $185,000 in San Francisco.

sections.content:
Pay climbs fastest for developers who combine modern frontend frameworks like React or Vue with solid backend fundamentals in Node.js, Python, or Go, plus cloud deployment skills on AWS or Azure. Experience with databases, API design, CI/CD pipelines, and infrastructure-as-code separates the $120,000 generalist from the $160,000-plus product engineer.

Specialization adds premiums: developers with DevOps depth, AI integration experience, or security awareness negotiate at the top of ranges. Soft skills matter too — owning features end to end, communicating with product teams, and mentoring juniors are the markers companies use to justify senior titles and the 30 to 50 percent raises that come with them.
